newsitem.title: USA: Southwestern PS merger costs seen hurting.
newsitem.headline: Southwestern PS merger costs seen hurting.

text.p: Southwestern Public Service Co said merger-related and business integration expenses are again expected to hurt earnings this year.
For the year ended August 31, the company Friday reported a 9.9 percent decline in earnings per share -- to $2.52 from $2.80 in fiscal 1995.

It noted 1995 earnings included gains for special items totaling $0.24 per share, while fiscal 1996 net included a gain on the sale of a unit of $0.19 per share. Merger-related and business integration expenses reduced profits in the latest year by $0.17 per share it said.

Assuming normal weather conditions, Southwestern PS said, it expects fiscal "1997 operating income will remain relatively flat, but that net earnings for 1997 will be negatively impacted by increased merger-related and business integration expenses."
The utility also said it has budgeted construction spending of $196.0 million, up sharply from 1996 outlays of $112.0 million which were up 18.3 percent from 1995.

The company also said Cabot Corp's September 30 sale of TUCO Inc to NexGen Resources Corp and Republic Financial Corp for $77 million plus net balance sheet adjustments "will benefit SPS customers, by reducing fuel costs within a few years by as much as $6 million annually."
TUCO owns the coal inventory at two coal-fueled power plants owned by Southwestern Public Service, which noted it spent about $375 million on fuel in 1995.
SPS previously, unsuccessfully, sought permission from the Public Utility Commission of Texas to purchase TUCO.
"The purchase by NexGen and Republic will offer our customers much of the advantage we had sought to provide them," Southwestern PS said.
